content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text does the thing the rule governs because it makes UNDERDETERMINED turn on a verse's not stating whose body is the channel.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"the phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' — I weighed (1) it forbids treating the silence of Acts 2:30 about the channel as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, against (2) it permits UNDERDETERMINED when a verse leaves the identity of the channel open.","why":"The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on Acts 2:30 not naming whose body is the channel, which is the prohibited use of a single verse's not stating a link as a ground."}
